refs.title: Published text configuration defaults
refs.detail: Reference defaults include 62 decoder layers, hidden width 8192, 128 Q heads, 16 KV heads, head size 64, 256 experts and eight routed picks. These values describe the public config class. Load the authorized pack’s actual config before allocating or selecting kernels.

refs.title: Muse Spark Open model card
refs.detail: The public model identity is 816B total / 42B active. The workshop did not qualify a particular gated checkpoint, tokenizer revision or memory representation.

refs.title: Reference router formula
refs.detail: Compute FP32 router projection and multiply by output_multiplier. Apply sigmoid. Rank by score plus e_score_correction_bias, gather unbiased scores, divide by their sum plus 1e−15 and multiply by routed_scaling_factor.

refs.title: SGLang fused Muse router
refs.detail: The operator binds correction bias, output multiplier, normalization epsilon and route scale. A specialization must preserve the reference’s expert membership and aligned weights.

refs.title: SGLang router fixtures
refs.detail: Upstream fixtures exercise (256,8) and (128,4). Test-case shapes describe the kernel suite and do not set checkpoint geometry.

refs.title: SGLang routed-only model guard
refs.detail: Muse’s OSS SGLang MoE rejects a nonzero num_shared_experts. Its forward path uses routed FFNs. An independent shared branch belongs to a different model contract.

refs.title: Expert activation and post-norm
refs.detail: Compute gate/up projections, activation product and down projection. Apply input-scaled RMSNorm to each expert output before multiplying its route weight and accumulating by original token row.

refs.title: Expert input and output projections
refs.detail: Router reads input at model width. A separate pre-expert projection and centered norm prepare expert-width inputs. Post-expert projection returns the combined output to model width.

refs.title: Centered and input-scaled RMSNorm
refs.detail: Centered RMSNorm normalizes then multiplies by 1 + learned weight. Input-scaled RMSNorm scales and rounds to input dtype before its reduction. Swapping those stages changes the result.

refs.title: Reference decoder boundaries
refs.detail: Apply attention pre-norm, attention, post-norm and learned residual gate. Repeat the corresponding boundary around the FFN. The stream handed to the next block includes both gated contributions.

refs.title: Learned residual gate
refs.detail: beta = sigmoid(g / T); alpha = sqrt(clamp(sigmoid(−g / T) × (1 + beta), min=eps)). The residual result is alpha × prior stream + beta × branch output.

refs.title: Muse attention output gate
refs.detail: Apply Q/K normalization, layer-dependent positional encoding, KV update and scaled attention. Normalize each output head, apply sigmoid of an input-dependent gate and then the output projection.

refs.title: Full and sliding attention defaults
refs.detail: The config derives a per-layer full/sliding mask pattern and RoPE/NoPE schedule if the checkpoint supplies no override. Read the actual layer arrays and cache window.

refs.title: Normalized token embeddings
refs.detail: Apply weightless RMSNorm to each gathered token embedding before the decoder stack.

refs.title: Vocabulary projection and softcap
refs.detail: The reference multiplies vocabulary logits by output_multiplier before the configured tanh softcap. Sampling consumes the transformed scores.

refs.title: Tokenizer and template inputs
refs.detail: The cache helper names tokenizer.json, tokenizer_config.json, chat_template.jinja and generation_config.json. Read the files from the chosen revision and compare the rendered prompt and token IDs.

refs.title: Muse text parsers
refs.detail: The SGLang recipe explicitly selects Muse reasoning and tool-call parsers. Enable these on the text interface only when the serving contract requests those outputs.

refs.title: Bounded expert residency design
refs.detail: Local workshop recommends an exact miss path and bounded resident set first. Evaluate cache policy on held-out traces, then qualify coalescing or prefetch against the target’s actual storage and memory budget. This is a construction requirement, not a measured Muse run.

refs.title: Checkpoint and capacity evidence
refs.detail: The workshop records the 816B/42B card and missing selected checkpoint bytes, tokenizer and accepted reference. Actual pack inventory and sustained access costs determine whether the target meets its memory and latency gates.

refs.title: Reference dense FFN
refs.detail: For a configured dense MLP layer the Muse reference computes activation(gate_proj(x)) times up_proj(x), followed by down_proj. The layer type in the selected configuration decides if this path runs.
